summary: Gas regularly turns up at HPL meters with no Sitara deal, with a deal whose term has ended, or parked on Strangers Gas. Logistics, Volume Management and accounting then email Daren Farmer's desk one meter at a time to get a ticket extended or created, and the reply often takes a day or more. A daily exception job would compare allocated flow against active Sitara deal terms and send each gap to the deal owner as a pre-filled extend/create/write-off request. This removes the manual detective work and the status-chasing, worth about $184 a month ($2,208 a year) at $85/hour, and closes gaps before payment and invoicing deadlines.

current_workflow.step: An allocation or exception screen shows flow at a meter on days with no valid deal. Examples are a meter allocated since March with no volume scheduled, or flow on days outside a deal's term.
The analyst looks up the Sitara deal ticket by hand, works out which days or months it does not cover, and decides who the trader or deal owner is.
To keep the volume from hanging in the exception screen, the analyst parks it on Strangers Gas or another temporary accounting arrangement.
The analyst emails the deal owner, usually Daren Farmer, asking for a specific deal to be extended (deal number, date and volume) or a new ticket to be created.
If nothing comes back, requesters send status follow-ups, forward the thread to other people, or escalate. This happens most when a payment or invoice deadline is close.

The deal owner or approver decides whether to extend the deal, create a new deal or a buy-back, or refuse/write the volume off (for example, very old or questionable volumes). Volumes are then reallocated, sometimes several times.
current_workflow.who: trader / deal owner, East desk, credit/approver

He will either need

solution.approach: A daily job pulls allocated and metered volumes by meter and day, along with active Sitara deal tickets (deal number, counterparty, meter, start and end dates, trader). It finds three exception types: flow with no deal, flow on days outside a deal's term, and volume sitting on Strangers Gas. For each one it builds an exception record showing the meter, the uncovered dates and volumes, the closest existing deal (the likely deal to extend) and the deal owner on record. The record goes to that owner as one daily digest. The digest has one-click options to extend the named deal, create a new deal, or refer the volume for write-off or investigation. The requesting analyst sees the status on a shared exception list, so they don't need to send status emails. Exceptions that are still open close to month-end, or close to a payment deadline, are escalated to the desk lead. Old ones are flagged early, before they become prior-year cleanups.
solution.trigger: Nightly schedule after the daily allocation load. An extra run happens on business days in the last week of the month and before settlement and payment cutoffs.
inputs: Daily allocated and metered volumes by meter and day (the data behind the allocation exception screen and Volume Management)
Active and recently expired Sitara deal tickets: deal number, counterparty, meter, term dates, trader/deal owner
Volumes currently assigned to the Strangers Gas contract
Unify paths/nominations for the meter, to tell unscheduled flow apart from scheduled flow
Payment and settlement deadlines for counterparties with pending payments
outputs: Daily exception digest for each deal owner (e.g. the HPL trader desk): meter, dates, uncovered volume, suggested deal to extend
Shared exception list with status (open, extension requested, extended, new deal, referred for write-off) for Volume Management, logistics and accounting
Escalation notice to the desk lead for exceptions that are still open near month-end or a payment cutoff
Monthly aging report of exceptions older than one production month, so prior-period cleanup is visible early
components: exception record store with status tracking
meter-to-deal-owner lookup table (maintained by the desk)
deal-owner daily digest email with extend / create / refer actions
shared exception list view for requesters

implementation_steps: Confirm read access to the allocation data behind Volume Management and to a Sitara deal extract (deal number, meter, term, trader). Use an export or report if there is no direct query.
Build the meter-to-deal-owner lookup from current Sitara traders. Have the desk confirm it, with a fallback owner for each pipeline or region.
Write the comparison job for the three exception types (no deal, outside term, Strangers Gas). Run it in report-only mode for one month against the emailed requests to check its precision.
Add the suggested-deal logic: the same meter and counterparty with a term that ends just before, or starts just after, the uncovered days.
Launch the deal-owner digest and the shared exception list. Ask Volume Management and logistics to point to the list instead of sending a new email for each meter.
Add escalation rules for exceptions still open near month-end close or near known payment cutoffs, plus the aging report.
After two production months, review the exceptions that were never resolved and tune the thresholds (for example, a minimum volume, and leaving out meters known to be measurement-only).
stays_manual: Choosing between extending a deal, creating a new deal or buy-back, or refusing the volume. This is a commercial and pricing decision for the trader.
Approving deals for old or suspicious volumes (e.g. a counterparty no longer in business, or volume found after nearly two years), which needs an investigation and approver sign-off.
Write-offs to unaccounted-for gas, or using an OBA/PPA for small or unreliable volumes. These need a judgment on how good the data is and how much money is at stake.
Entering or changing Unify paths for cross-desk (e.g. East desk) pieces, which need coordination between desks.
Pricing on newly created or extended deals.
risks: The evidence does not show the actual data feeds or table structures for allocations or Sitara. Feasibility of the extract has to be confirmed before committing; plan a manual export fallback.

Deal-owner records may be stale or ambiguous (requesters often ask who should be rolling a deal). If the lookup is not kept up to date, exceptions go to the wrong person. Mitigate with a fallback owner and a weekly 'unowned' list.
Meter allocation data is revised after the fact, so the flags can be false or keep changing. Show the allocation date and suppress repeats until the volume changes.
Too many small exceptions (single-day, tiny volumes) could make owners ignore the digest. Use a volume threshold and grouping by deal.
The savings estimate (about $184/month) uses the median handling time across all messages. The real benefit depends on whether requesters actually stop sending ad-hoc emails.
The evidence comes from one mailbox (farmer-d), so the volume handled by other desks is not visible.
success_metric: Number of meter/day exceptions with flow but no valid Sitara deal (or on Strangers Gas) still open at month-end close, and median days from first flow to deal extension or creation. Track the count of ad-hoc 'please extend deal' emails to the deal desk alongside these.
